Revised assessment: The statement acknowledges a severe negative real shock from the coronavirus, with downside risks to activity and muted inflation—conditions under which the literature supports forceful, countercyclical easing. With the policy rate at the effective lower bound and large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, the Fed is deploying balance-sheet tools that, per VAR and narrative evidence (Sims; Romer and Romer), can support output by lowering term premia and stabilizing financial conditions. Consistent with the credit channel literature (Oliner and Rudebusch; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Gertler and Gilchrist), the suite of liquidity facilities, discount-window easing, and bank capital/liquidity-buffer relief should help sustain credit supply, especially to borrowers most sensitive to external finance premia. The statement also notes subdued inflation expectations; anchoring expectations around the 2 percent objective via forward guidance aligns with inflation-forecast targeting insights (Svensson) and the broader New Keynesian emphasis on expectations. Overall, while the near-term macro tone is negative due to the pandemic shock, the policy response meaningfully mitigates the downside relative to inaction.
